newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Aziz meets Kalmykian republic president.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Aziz meets Kalmykian republic president.

text.p: Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz met the president of Russia's ethnic republic of Kalmykia, Kirsan Ilyumzhinov, Iraqi newspapers reported on Sunday.

"Aziz appreciates Russia and its Duma's (parliament) efforts to lift the unjust embargo," al-Thawra, the newspaper of the ruling Baath party, said, adding that Ilyumzhinov called for an end to U.N. sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Aziz was in Moscow earlier this month to seek Russia's help in having the curbs removed.
Moscow wants an immediate lifting of the sanctions to revive its once lucrative trade with Baghdad.
Iraq signed an oil deal with Russia in March allowing Russian firms to develop seven to eight billion barrels of reserves in Iraq's southern Qurana oilfield.
The U.N. sanctions ban oil investments but Russian officials said the contract would not start before the end of the curbs.
A team of Russian politicians and businessmen is in Baghdad seeking better ties and business links under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
The deal, which went into effect in December, allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy urgent needs for Iraqis.
